To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Ss can encode verbal material pictorially, (2) Ss can do so in a manner that is consistent with their expectations of the task, and (3) the encoding modality is determined in part by the modality of subsequent material.

(a) Ss encode material in the modality they anticipate will be used in the response, and (b) Ss are more likely to encode material pictorially when the material is verbal and to encode material verbally when it is pictorial.
the reaction times to the “different” responses are longer when the first stimulus is encoded in a modality different from that of the second stimulus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether or not the way in which material is encoded in memory is dependent on the S’s expectation of the way the information is to be used.
the question of how Ss encode information.
the effects of S’s expectation of the use to which the material will be put on the modality of encoding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the encoding of a stimulus is not a function of its own modality, but of the modality which S expects to be used.
encoding is determined by S’s expectations of how he is to use the material.
encoding of the stimulus material is determined by S’s expectations of how the material is to be used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
encoding is a function of the way the information is to be used.
S’s expectations of what he is about to do with a set of stimuli determine what he encodes.
the encoding modality is not a property of a stimulus but is dependent on the S’s anticipation of the task he is to do on the material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the way we encode information in memory is dependent on our expectations of what we are going to do with the information.
the encoding process is not automatic and that the way S’s encode the stimuli can be manipulated.
encoding is not a passive process, but an active process that is influenced by S’s expectations.
